title: Responses compatibility adapter: edge-case mapping and backcompat strategy
creator: Diego Martinez
description: Build an adapter layer that accepts the OpenAI Responses API request/response shapes and semantics and maps them to Redwood's internal request model and streaming events. This enables customers using OpenAI-style client libraries to target Redwood endpoints with minimal code change while preserving Redwood features: robust streaming, structured output validation, function/tool calling, and rollout/backoff policies. The adapter must document incompatibilities and provide a header-driven compatibility mode (best-effort vs strict).
acceptance_criteria: Adapter accepts OpenAI Responses-like payloads (messages, content, functions, function_call) and returns equivalent Redwood response objects or streaming events.
Streaming: partial token events and function call deltas are emitted to clients in the same order OpenAI expects, without dropping tokens.

Function/tool calling: when a model requests a function, the adapter emits a tool invocation event compatible with Redwood tooling and returns the tool result as a structured function response to the client.
Structured outputs: JSON schema validation is applied to structured output and validation errors surfaced incrementally during streaming when possible.
Backcompat modes: header X-Redwood-Compat: openai-best-effort and openai-strict are respected; strict mode fails fast on unmappable features.
Performance: adapter overhead adds <5ms p50 and <15ms p95 on token emission in the common path (tested on staging workload).
Tests: unit + e2e adapter tests cover typical OpenAI client flows, streaming tool-calls, and malformed function schemas; test harness and migration guide merged into docs repo.
work_log: 2025-01-18: Kickoff — scoped list of OpenAI Responses features to support (messages, content, role, function_call, function definitions, streaming deltas); Diego and Karen drafted initial mapping doc.

2025-01-22: Prototype shim implemented in runtime proxy (golang) that translates OpenAI messages -> Redwood messages; basic streaming preserved as chunked events; initial benchmarks run against toy model (latency + CPU).

2025-01-24: Design review with SDK and Product (Aisha Rahman, Tom Becker) — agreed to support two compatibility modes and surface an explicit migration guide. Product requested opt-in header rather than global toggle.

2025-01-28: Edge-case discovered: OpenAI allows a model to issue a function_call with partial arguments across multiple streamed deltas. Decided to buffer function_call argument fragments until a terminal delta or a configurable timeout (default 200ms).

2025-01-29: Security review checkpoint — KMS and audit implications for tool outputs discussed with Security (Maya Patel). Decided to annotate adapter logs with original request id and redact PII in stored arguments per private deployment policy.
2025-01-31: Benchmarks vs baseline: adapter p95 token emission overhead = 12ms on i3.large staging; memory overhead acceptable. Need micro-optimizations to reach goal.
2025-02-02: PR opened for adapter code and integration tests; awaiting eng-review. Added e2e scenarios for streaming JSON schema fragments.
decisions: Expose two compatibility modes via header X-Redwood-Compat: 'openai-best-effort' (default) and 'openai-strict'.
Buffer partial function_call argument deltas for up to 200ms before emitting a tool invocation to allow streaming fragments to complete; provide a config knob for dedicated/private deployments.
Emit structured output validation events as 'structured.validation' to SDKs so UIs can render progressive validation feedback without breaking token stream order.
In strict mode, unmappable features (e.g., OpenAI response types we cannot represent) return a 422 with a descriptive error and a compatibility-report header pointing to remediation steps.
Adapter will not attempt to emulate model-level fallback policies; customers must express routing/fallback via Redwood routing config — add docs for translation patterns.
open_questions: How should multiple sequential function calls within a single response be represented to existing OpenAI clients that expect a single 'function_call' object? (temporary approach: emit sequential function_call events with stable invocation ids).
Do we need a formal schema for streaming validation events, or are ad-hoc text-coded events sufficient for SDK teams? (SDKs prefer a small schema; follow-up with DX).

Should adapter perform any automated sanitization of function arguments before logging, or rely on caller-provided sanitization? Security prefers conservative redaction, Product prefers caller control.
Edge-case: models that rely on OpenAI-specific 'tool' metadata fields — map to Redwood tool metadata if present, otherwise attach mapping hints in compatibility-report header.
testing_plan: Unit tests: mapping functions for messages -> internal model, function definitions -> tool descriptors, and streaming assembler/buffer behavior.
Integration tests: run real OpenAI client library (node/python) against adapter in staging; assert client receives expected streamed deltas and function_call events.
Load test: reproduce 1000 concurrent streaming sessions with typical chat lengths to measure p95 emission latency and memory pressure.
Security tests: verify PII redaction paths, KMS access patterns for tool outputs, and audit log annotations for adapter-translated requests.
Migration tests: run sample apps (chat widget, tool-execution bot) against adapter with both compat modes and compare output against native Redwood API.
prs: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk-js/pull/213 — SDK event schema changes for structured.validation
next_steps: Finish micro-optimizations to bring p95 token emission <10ms (profiling + hotpath rewrite).
Address SDK feedback: propose small schema for streaming validation events and land SDK changes in sync with adapter.
Complete security review and update redaction config defaults for public vs private deployments.
Prepare rollout plan: enable adapter behind feature flag for Hosted customers, offer Private deployments opt-in, and publish migration guide and sample patches for popular OpenAI client libs.
Schedule canary for runtime-2.0 with a single internal team and monitor for missing token/delta regressions before wider activation.
